haiku-low.q1: No. Accepted cursor updates go to the cursor Lua script in Redis. They never pass through the document service and never reach Postgres.
haiku-low.q2: Clients send at most once per 60 ms. The node silently drops any cursor arriving under 50 ms after the last accepted cursor on that connection.
haiku-low.q3: It stores the cursor as held and draws nothing. After each applied remote op, it draws the held cursor once its rev is at or below appliedRev.
haiku-low.q4: It draws at transformPosition(pos, rev, appliedRev). If that throws HistoryGone (older than the 500-revision history), the position is dropped and the caret hidden until the next update.
haiku-low.q5: One user shows one caret, the tab that moved last, though each tab has its own entry. The user disappears only when their last entry is removed, by clean leave or expiry.
haiku-low.q6: After a clean tab close, others see the change within 2 s. After the gateway node dies, users leave everyone's list within 45 s, about 35 s at most.
haiku-low.q7: In Redis primary: one ZSET pres:{docId} with userId|connId entries scored by expiry, plus HASH cur:{docId}. Each entry is refreshed by touch every 10 s, expiring 30 s after the last touch.
haiku-low.q8: A sweeping node's reap script removes entries past expiry every 5 s. If the user has no entry left, it publishes leave on pres:{docId}, which reaches other clients via their nodes.
haiku-low.q9: The cursor script publishes on pres:{docId}, and every subscribed node forwards it to local sockets. The sender's own cursor is never sent back to the sender, but the sender's node still forwards it to other local viewers.
haiku-low.q10: The node subscribes to pres:{docId} before join, sets minV to the snapshot's n, and forwards only v > minV. The client applies later events only if v > snapshot.n.
haiku-low.q11: The join snapshot includes each user's last cursor from the cur:{docId} hash, so idle users' carets come with the snapshot.
haiku-low.q12: Each cursor carries a per-document counter v. The client keeps lastV[user] and drops any cursor with v at or below it, so older out-of-order cursors are discarded.

sonnet.q1: No. Accepted cursors go to the `cursor` Lua script in Redis; they never go through the document service and never reach Postgres (nothing about presence or cursors is ever written to Postgres).
sonnet.q2: At most one per 60 ms from the client (trailing send always goes out, plus one re-send 1 s after the last move). The node requires at least 50 ms since the last accepted cursor on that connection (monotonic clock) and silently drops faster ones.
sonnet.q3: It holds the cursor (rev > appliedRev) and draws nothing. After each applied remote op, it draws any held cursor whose rev <= appliedRev.
sonnet.q4: If rev < appliedRev, it draws at transformPosition(pos, rev, appliedRev). If that throws HistoryGone (rev older than the last 500 revisions kept), it drops the position and hides the caret until the next update. On every applied op, drawn carets are re-transformed from their atRev.
sonnet.q5: One user with two tabs has one userId and two connIds (two entries) but one presence listing and one shared caret (the tab that moved last). The join is published only for the first entry, and leave only when the user's last entry goes, so they disappear only when all their entries are gone (both tabs closed, or expired/reaped).
sonnet.q6: Clean tab close: within 2 s. Node death: within 45 s limit (at most 35 s in practice: 30 s expiry plus up to 5 s until next sweep).
sonnet.q7: In the Redis primary, per document: `pres:{docId}` ZSET with one `userId|connId` entry per connection (score = expiry in ms), and `cur:{docId}` HASH holding `_n`, cursors and profiles. Entries are kept fresh by `touch` every 10 s, which sets the score to Redis TIME + 30 s (and EXPIRE 120); there is also a 120 s key TTL.
sonnet.q8: Nothing from the dead node; its entries stop being touched and expire. A `reap` script run by another node's 5 s sweep removes entries with expired scores and, if the user has no other entry, deletes their c:/p: fields and publishes `leave` on `pres:{docId}`. Subscribed nodes forward it to their clients (presence_leave). If every node on the doc died, the 120 s key TTL deletes the keys.
sonnet.q9: The node runs the `cursor` script, which publishes the cursor event on Redis pub/sub `pres:{docId}`. Every subscribed node, including the sender's own node, receives it and forwards to its local sockets, except it is never sent back to the user who sent it. A viewer on the sender's node (other than the sender) gets it via the same pub/sub path (the node forwards only events with v > that connection's minV).
sonnet.q10: The node subscribes to `pres:{docId}` first, then runs the atomic `join` script, which returns a snapshot with the current n. The node sets conn.minV = n and forwards only events with v > minV; the client applies later events only if v > snapshot.n. Events already in the snapshot are dropped as duplicates, and later ones are applied.
sonnet.q11: Cursors are also stored in the `cur:{docId}` hash (`c:<userId>` = {rev,pos,v}), and the join snapshot includes everyone's last cursors, so the idle user's caret appears (held until the client reaches that rev if needed).
sonnet.q12: Each cursor event carries a per-document version `v`; the client keeps `lastV[user]` and drops any cursor with v <= lastV[user], whatever order messages arrive in. Only the newest cursor per user is kept.
